newsitem.title: USA: Japan-US firms must lower trade tension - Japan exec.
newsitem.headline: Japan-US firms must lower trade tension - Japan exec.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp, Chairman Shoichiro Toyoda said he hopes the private sectors of the United States and Japan can learn to work together to ease trade frictions without government intervention.

Toyoda, speaking as chairman of Japan's Federation of Economic Organizations, or Keidanren, told a group of business leaders from Japan and southern U.S. states that he expects frictions to continue as the economies of the two countries become increasingly intertwined.
"We must do our best to resolve these frictions in the private sector before they become politicized," Toyoda said.
Toyoda has been a vocal supporter of wide-ranging reforms in Japan to boost its sagging economy.

"To be sure, deregulation will be disruptive for companies that relied on government regulation," he said through a translator. "But Japanese society will lose its vitality if we leave in place a web of regulations."
Toyoda said the auto maker, which has the capacity to build 1 million vehicles a year in North America, currently has no plans to add new plants in the United States.

Toyota in May broke ground on a new $700 million truck plant in Indiana and announced plans to build a $198 million engine plant in West Virginia as it seeks to boost capacity in North America to 1.2 million vehicles a year by 1998.
